title: Banded latency‑hedging admission with stitching fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a banded admission controller that combines latency hedging, per-tenant soft budgets, and response stitching fallbacks to maintain tail latency SLOs across regions during capacity churn and partial outages. The goal is to reduce P95/P99 latency violations for text-generation and chat endpoints while preserving useful output for degraded requests rather than failing hard.
motivation: We see recurring tail latency SLO violations during multi-region failover and bursty traffic to popular tenants. Current hard-shed behavior causes many customer-facing errors and increases support tickets. A strategy that admits requests into graded bands, applies hedging to short‑circuit slow replicas, and, when necessary, stitches partial outputs (prefix-only responses, token-drop compensation) will preserve perceived availability and reduce error rates.
goals: Reduce P99 latency violations by 40% for impacted regions during failover windows
Avoid hard 5xx failures for best-effort customers by returning graceful degraded responses 90% of the time
Provide per-tenant soft budget accounting to prioritize critical customers without starvation
Expose observability and tracing to measure admission decisions and stitch events
non_goals: Full rewrite of serving runtime—this is admission/routing layer and stitch hooks only
Changing model internals or tokenization logic beyond minimal trimming policies
proposal_summary: Implement a Banded Admission Controller (BAC) that assigns incoming requests to a: Hot band (low-latency SLO, reserved tokens), Warm band (best-effort with hedging), Cold band (queue/trim/stitch or cheap model variant). Integrate with existing circuit breaker signals and per-tenant token budgets. Add a lightweight response stitching service that can combine prefix cached outputs with truncated generation and mark responses with degradation metadata.
implementation_notes: Admission tiers: define three bands with configurable thresholds and weights per region
Per-tenant soft budgets tracked in Redis with leaky-bucket semantics; budgets refill with adjustable rates
Latency hedging: submit duplicate hedged requests to fast-path replicas after X ms; cancel slower path if fast returns
Circuit breaker hooks: use existing CB events to trigger immediate band migration for affected replicas
Response stitching: service reads KV cache for prefix tokens and requests short-run generation for suffix; if suffix times out, return prefix+marker and synthetic summary token
Config: feature-flagged rollout using console targets and canary percentage by tenant
Telemetry: emit admission_decision, band, budget_hit, hedged_request_id, stitch_event, degraded_reason as tags on traces and metrics
workplan: Design review with runtime and console teams (week 1)
Prototype admission controller in shadow mode (week 2)
Implement per-tenant budgeting and integrate hedging (week 3)
Build response stitching microservice and stitch hooks (week 4)
Run chaos tests for multi-region failover scenarios (week 5)
Canary rollout: 5% tenants, observe metrics, iterate (week 6)
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic shows <10% increase in token cost vs baseline while P99 decreases by >=30%
Degraded responses contain stitch metadata and are parsable by SDKs/documented
Feature flag can disable BAC without traffic loss or required restart
No regression in throughput for dedicated pools (verified by load tests)
risks: Stitching may create confusing partial outputs for downstream parsers if schema not standardized
Per-tenant budgets risk starving small tenants if misconfigured; requires safe defaults
Hedging duplicates increase GPU load; must be rate-limited and adaptive
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission decision logic
Integration test with hedging disabled/enabled in staging
Chaos monkey failover test simulating regional network partitions
A/B test comparing current shedder vs BAC under synthetic burst workloads
observability: Dashboards: Admission band distribution, budget consumption by tenant, stitch rates, hedged success ratio
Alerts: sustained >5% rate of hard sheds, stitch failure increase, hedged cancellation anomaly
Logs: structured admission events with correlation IDs
rollout_strategy: Start in shadow mode for 48 hours to validate decision distributions, then enable for low‑impact tenants (5%). If metrics stable, ramp to 25% and run targeted chaos tests before global enable. Provide emergency kill switch in console tied to feature flag and circuit-breaker auto-disable path.
open_questions: What are safe default refill rates for per-tenant budgets across SKU tiers?
Should hedging be limited to Warm band only or configurable per-model?
How to surface stitch degradation in client SDKs so apps can adapt gracefully?
